title: ICU 72h readmission model weekly retraining control graph

root_goal.statement: Keep the deployed ICU 72-hour readmission risk model at least as accurate, calibrated and fair on future, unseen ICU discharges as the current model, without unsafe automatic replacement.
root_goal.observable_success: On a frozen, time-forward holdout (discharges after the training window, with 72h follow-up complete, never seen by the trainer), the candidate shows AUC improvement >= pre-registered margin with CI lower bound > 0, calibration slope 0.8-1.2 and Brier not worse, no subgroup AUC drop > 0.03, and post-deployment shadow/prospective monitoring confirms it; Bruce signs each production swap.
out_of_scope: Evaluating AUC on the same month used for training (in-sample AUC is not acceptance evidence)
Automatic replacement of the production model without human sign-off
Changing the outcome definition (72h ICU readmission), label window or acceptance thresholds by the agent
Clinical decision changes driven by the model without clinical governance

classification_rationale: The brief as written is a single loop whose verifier (same-month AUC) is produced from the optimizer's own training data, so it is gameable and will select overfit models; auto-swap is a high-risk clinical side effect. A safe design needs an execution loop plus independent temporal-holdout verification, counter-metrics (calibration, subgroup, drift), an audit of data/label provenance, arbitration of conflicting signals and a human gate before deployment, with weekly vs monthly vs quarterly cadences. Hence graph_plus_loop.

allowed_actions: Read de-identified ICU training extracts for the rolling training window
Train and tune candidate models in a sandbox
Write candidate model artifacts and training reports to the candidate registry
Propose threshold or anchor changes to governance
forbidden_actions: Read or query the temporal holdout set or its labels
Compute acceptance AUC on training data
Deploy or replace the production model
Modify evaluation code, acceptance thresholds, holdout definition or outcome definition
Delete or suppress failed candidate results

frozen_rules: Acceptance evidence comes only from the time-forward holdout: discharges strictly after the training window with complete 72h follow-up, held by the evaluation service, inaccessible to the trainer
Outcome definition (unplanned ICU readmission within 72h of ICU discharge) and label lag are frozen
Pre-registered acceptance thresholds: AUC delta margin with bootstrap CI lower bound > 0, calibration slope 0.8-1.2, Brier non-inferior, subgroup AUC drop <= 0.03
Production swap requires Bruce's signed approval and a rollback plan; previous model kept warm
Evaluation code is versioned and hashed; trainer has no write access

failure_policy.failed: Keep current production model; log candidate failure with evidence; next weekly cycle starts fresh
failure_policy.blocked: If holdout labels are incomplete, stale or data pipeline audit fails, freeze retraining and escalate to Bruce
failure_policy.budget_exhausted: Stop tuning, report best candidate as not-promoted, keep production model

conditions: completed: candidate passed holdout, counter-metric and audit checks and Bruce approved swap (or rejected it)
failed: candidate did not beat production on holdout; production unchanged
blocked: holdout stale/contaminated or provenance audit failed
budget_exhausted: retry/compute budget used without an acceptable candidate

arbitration.priority_policy: Patient safety and calibration > subgroup fairness > data provenance integrity > holdout AUC gain > retraining cadence. Any veto from verification, counter-metric or audit blocks promotion; an AUC gain never overrides a safety/calibration/fairness veto.

verification.independence_statement: The holdout evaluator is a separate deterministic service with its own frozen code, reading time-forward discharges and labels from the EHR outcome registry that the trainer cannot read; the provenance auditor reads raw EHR admission/discharge records independently of the training extract.

checks.criterion: AUC delta CI lower bound > 0 vs production on time-forward holdout
Holdout verifier gates on AUC; calibration/fairness/drift vetoes come from counter_metrics node
Provenance audit report must be clean (leakage, label definition) before holdout verdict is accepted

anchors.source: EHR outcome registry: ICU discharges in the week(s) after the training window with complete 72h follow-up
anchors.evidence_form: Frozen time-forward holdout set with observed 72h readmission labels, hash-registered
anchors.freshness_rule: Rebuilt weekly from discharges after training cutoff; must have complete 72h follow-up; invalid if any overlap with training window

nodes.responsibility: Provide frozen, trainer-inaccessible time-forward holdout with observed labels
Weekly retrain candidate on rolling last-month ICU extract within sandbox; report in-sample metrics only as diagnostics
Score candidate and production model on frozen holdout with frozen code; bootstrap AUC delta; veto if not superior
Check calibration, Brier, subgroup AUC gaps, alert-rate/PPV at operating threshold and covariate drift on holdout; veto cheap AUC wins
Monthly audit of label definition, leakage between training and holdout, cohort shifts and pipeline changes against raw EHR ADT records; post-deployment prospective performance review
Combine verifier, counter-metric and audit verdicts under priority policy into promote / hold recommendation
nodes.priority_policy: Safety/calibration > fairness > provenance > AUC gain; any veto blocks promotion

nodes.responsibility: Quarterly review of thresholds, holdout design, outcome definition and whether the model still serves the clinical goal; proposals require Bruce approval
Bruce signs or rejects the production swap based on arbiter recommendation and vetoes
Execute approved swap: shadow run, canary, full rollout, with automatic rollback to warm previous model on monitoring alarm
Record terminal state and hand off weekly report
